Subject: Redwood DPA redlines and subprocessors appendix

Claire / Vanessa,

I reviewed the attached redline and added a couple of edits for clarity and risk allocation. Key points:

- Subprocessors: we will provide an up-to-date public table of subprocessors and a contractual commitment to notify Bluepoint 30 days prior to onboarding new subprocessors. I added an appendix reference that lists current subprocessors and processing locations — please review.

- Cross-border transfers: we accept SCCs where applicable; for customers with EU residency requirements we include an addendum that references EU SCCs and a DTA (data transfer addendum).

- Encryption / key custody: our standard for Dedicated is that Redwood manages runtime encryption keys unless the customer elects a Private deployment with customer KMS. I flagged the language where Bluepoint had requested "customer-only key custody" in Dedicated (Monica’s note: that is typically only feasible in Private/VPC or on-prem).

- Logs & retention: Redwood retains request-level operational logs for reconciliation and incident response; retention period is configurable but default is 90 days. I added explicit retention and deletion clauses and a bit on audit access. If Bluepoint needs a shorter retention period, we can add a contractual SLA and a technical config for Dedicated.

Attachments: DPA_Bluepoint_Redlines_Monica.docx (redline with comments).

Please have Bluepoint legal confirm: 1) they are comfortable with notification cadence for subprocessors; 2) whether they will sign the Dedicated DPA (Redwood-managed keys) or require Private/VPC addendum (customer key custody).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_Bluepoint_Redlines_Monica.docx]

Claire / Tom — copying Laura from Legal Ops. I attached the one-page matrix (Dedicated_vs_Private-OnePager.pdf) that covers the five items you asked about. Short answers here:

- Data-at-rest responsibility: Dedicated = Redwood is responsible for storage infrastructure and snapshot lifecycle; Private/VPC = customer is responsible for the host environment.
- Encryption key ownership: Dedicated = Redwood-managed keys by default; Private = optional customer-managed KMS with customer key custody.
- Audit logs: Redwood provides configurable access; default retention 90 days; can contract for shorter/longer retention.
- Backups: Redwood maintains encrypted backups; retention follows retention policy; Private deployments can opt to disable Redwood backups.
- Export controls: both modes follow the same export-control screening process and contractual representations; location of processing can be restricted via region tag.

Laura will send the Adobe Sign envelope today. Tom, please confirm the preferred signer name and email on your side.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
